utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to everybody. With all due respect and gratitude for the people who will be translating this simultaneously, I ask Madam Registrar to please announce the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-41-PT, the Prosecutor versus Pasko Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. First of all, the appearances, please. Mr. Harmon first, please, who will have to leave in 15 minutes, if I understood you properly. We will all attempt to be as brief as possible, to work as fast as possible. But regardless of that, we have to -- [In English] So please would you give the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My name is Mark Harmon. I represent the Prosecutor's Office. So appearing with me today to my right is Magda Karagiannakis, also representing the Prosecutor's Office, and particularly after I leave should this proceeding go back twenty minutes to 3.00. To my left is Ms. Kamala Janakiram. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Et maintenant je tourne a la Defense.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. My name is Tomislav Jonjic, and I will be representing the accused Pasko Ljubicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please sit down. I would specify that I am Judge El Mahdi. I have been designated to Chamber 1 by the order of 3 December 2001. I am a Pre-Trial Judge. I am wishing you good day. Can you hear me in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can follow all the debates in a language which you can understand.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can understand completely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to be very brief. Today's hearing will be devoted to permit the Defence, and more exactly to permit the accused, to be apprised of the modified, amended indictment. As you know - and now I am addressing counsel for Defence - you have apprised Mr. Ljubicic of the fact that the initial indictment has been amended in the sense of a better organisation of the indictment, which should enable a better understanding of the facts and the counts of the case so that the accused may have a better defence, an opportunity to defend himself better. Therefore, this is not a new indictment. This is a modified or reorganised indictment in order to better protect the rights of Defence. I think, Mr. Jonjic, that I have spoken about what the meaning is of this amended indictment and what this new presentation of this indictment means. And today we are here to give to your client the possibility, a new occasion, to -- it seems that there is a sound problem. It seems that there is a sound problem. Can you hear me, Mr. Jonjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you will have had an opportunity to speak to your client and to explain to him what is the meaning of the new or modified indictment so that he is in a position today to argue his case, to plead. I know -- I am aware of the fact that he had pleaded initially and that there were no new counts brought. But the formulation and the organisation, the structure of the new indictment resulted, finally, in the fact that the counts are now 15 instead of 11. But the charges are the same, in a more detailed form, in a way which should enable the Defence and in the opinion of the Chamber to better prepare its case. Therefore, I want to be sure that your client is apprised of what it means, this amendment of the indictment, and that he is ready today to plead about the charges either in the form of the principal formulation, as it was, or in the present drafting of the indictment, as it is modified now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- The 15th of April in accordance with the motion, according to Rule 72, the accused has received the indictment in the language that he understands. In the meantime, he has of course consulted with his attorney and today he is prepared to plead whether he's guilty or not guilty. If you allow me just for a moment to respond to a question before you have even asked me this question. I spoke about this with my learned friend Mr. Harmon, because he's in a hurry, in order to be as expedient as possible, we have agreed that it is not necessary to read the indictment. So this is all that the Defence wishes to state at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I wish to congratulate the parties for having agreed this way and to have -- for having cooperated. This collaboration seems to have been established between the parties. So Mr. Ljubicic, please, I am now going to ask to the court registrar to read the indictment, the counts, and you will now have an opportunity to plead. Do you hear me? Can you hear me? Can you hear me, Mr. Ljubicic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I repeat what I was saying. I am going to now ask the court clerk to read the indictment, and you will have the possibility to plead guilty or not guilty for each charge which is now in the new indictment. So Madam Court Registrar, could you please read the counts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1: Persecutions on political, racial, or religious grounds, a crime against humanity, as recognised by Articles 5(h), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Ljubicic? Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters find it difficult to hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat. You haven't been heard.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, for count 2.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2: An unlawful attack on civilians, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Articles 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and customary law, Article 51(2) of the Additional Protocol I and Article 13(2) of Additional Protocol II of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar, next count.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 3: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Articles 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, Count 4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 4: Murder, a crime against humanity, as recognised by Articles 5(a), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam Registrar, count 5.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 5: Violence to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Article 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 6: Inhumane acts, a crime against humanity as recognised by Article 5(i), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Ljubicic, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 7: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by articles 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 8: Murder, a crime against humanity, as recognised by Articles 5(a), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 9: Violence to life and person, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Article 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Ljubicic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 10: Inhumane acts, a crime against humanity as recognised by Article 5(i), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Ljubicic, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, will you please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 11: Devastation not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or custom of war, as recognised by Articles 3(b), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Ljubicic, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 12: Destruction or wilful damage to institutions dedicated to religion or education, a violation of the laws or custom of war, as recognised by Articles 3(d), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 13: Plunder of public or private property, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Articles 3(e), 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ljubicic. Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 14: Cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Articles 3, 7(1), and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ljubicic. Madam, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 15: Inhumane acts, a crime against humanity as recognised by Article 5(i), 7(1) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ljubicic, how do you plead, guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ljubicic. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can remain seated. I would like to specify that you have a right to hear the reading of the indictment as a whole and that the decision which has been made to read only the counts was with the consent of your Defence counsel, which means that you approve the fact that only the counts will have been read out to you and that you have approved this procedure, if I understand matters well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that we should proceed this way. I am familiar with the entire indictment, and I agree to act in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir. Now that we have finished this phase of argument and that Mr. Ljubicic has pleaded not guilty, I will now address the parties and ask if they have anything to add, any remarks to make before we start our Status Conference. I will first ask Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have nothing to add, Judge El Mahdi. I must now excuse myself with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. [Interpretation] For the Defence, do you have anything to add before we start the Status Conference?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we do not have anything at this point, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Jonjic. Madam Registrar, could we proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: adjourned at 2.41 p.m., to be followed by a Status Conference.
